{{nihongo|'''Minume Shrine'''|敏馬神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Iwaya Nakamachi|Q11474374|qid=Q11474374}}, {{ill|Nada-ku, Kobe|Q1154555|qid=Q1154555}}, {{ill|Kobe|af|Kobe|an|Kobe|ar|كوبه|arz|كوبه|ast|Kōbe|az|Kobe|azb|کوبه، هیوقو|ban|Kobé|be|Кобэ|be_x_old|Кобэ|bg|Кобе|bn|কৌবে|br|Kobe|ca|Kobe|ce|Кобе|ceb|Kobe (kapital sa prepektura)|ckb|کۆبێ|cs|Kóbe|cy|Kobe|da|Kobe|de|Kōbe|el|Κόμπε|eo|Kobeo|es|Kōbe|et|Kōbe|eu|Kobe|ext|Kobe|fa|کوبه (شهر)|fi|Kōbe|fj|Kobe|fo|Kobe|fr|Kobe|frr|Kōbe|ga|Kōbe|gd|Kobe|gl|Kōbe|ha|Kobe|he|קובה (יפן)|hi|कोबे|hr|Kobe|hu|Kóbe|hy|Կոբե|id|Kota Kobe|io|Kobe|is|Kobe|it|Kōbe|ja|神戸市|ka|კობე|kab|Kobe|ki|Kobe|ko|고베시|ky|Кобе|lg|Kobe japan|li|Kobe|lmo|Kōbe|lt|Kobė|lv|Kobe|mg|Kobe|mi|Kobe|ml|കോബെ|mn|Кобэ|mr|कोबे|ms|Kobe|mt|Kōbe|my|ကိုးဘေးမြို့|mzn|کوبه|nl|Kobe|nn|Kobe|no|Kobe|oc|Kobe|os|Кобе|pa|ਕੋਬੇ|pl|Kobe|pms|Kobe|pnb|کوبے|pnt|Κόμπε|pt|Kobe|qu|Kōbe|ro|Kobe|ru|Кобе|sc|Kōbe|sco|Kobe|sh|Kobe|simple|Kobe, Hyōgo|sk|Kóbe|sl|Kobe|sr|Кобе|su|Kobe|sv|Kobe|sw|Kobe, Hyogo|szl|Kobe|ta|கோபே|tg|Кобе|th|โคเบะ|tl|Kobe|tr|Kobe|tt|Кобе|tum|Kobe|tw|Kobe|ug|Kobe|uk|Кобе|ur|کوبے|uz|Kobe|vep|Kobe (lidn)|vi|Kōbe|war|Kobe|wuu|神户市|zea|Kobe|zh|神户市|zh_classical|神戶市|zh_min_nan|Kôbe-chhī|zh_yue|神戶|qid=Q48320}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was prefectural shrine. {{nihongo|'''Minume Shrine'''|敏馬神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

It stands on a hill north of where {{ill|Japan National Route 2|Q1131340|qid=Q1131340}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 43|Q6157520|qid=Q6157520}} run together east-west. About 150 m southeast of {{ill|Iwaya Station (Hyōgo)|Q6100854|qid=Q6100854|lt=Iwaya Station}} on Hanshin.

== Enshrined deity ==
In old writings, Minume was also written as 汶売, 美奴売, 三犬女, 見宿女, etc.

Now the main deity is {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, with {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Kōtaishin}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano no Imasu Kami}} as associated deities; until the Edo period it was called “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gozu Tennō}}.”

The original deity was Minume-no-Kami (美奴売神 / 敏馬神). From the name, Minume-no-Kami is considered the same as the water deity {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mitsuha-no-me-no-Kami}}, now enshrined in the precinct water shrine. There is a well called Akai or Miro-me Shimizu. The view that this goddess gave her name to Minume is considered strongest. Another theory, likely inspired by {{ill|Kakinomoto no Hitomaro|Q380818|qid=Q380818}}’s poem “Passing Minume where seaweed is harvested...,” derives it from miru ({{ill|Codium fragile|Q2712208|qid=Q2712208|lt=miru}}), used in making sea-salt.

== History ==
An excerpt of ''Settsu no Kuni Fudoki'' records this shrine’s foundation. When {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} departed for conquest of Silla, she prayed for victory at Kamisaki Matsubara in {{ill|Kawabe District, Hyōgo|Q1042053|qid=Q1042053}} (present {{ill|Kanzaki|Q11589609|qid=Q11589609|lt=Kanzaki}} in {{ill|Amagasaki|Q213318|qid=Q213318}} or {{ill|Toyonaka|Q467479|qid=Q467479}}). A deity from Minume-yama in Nose upstream on the {{ill|Ina River|Q11571867|qid=Q11571867}} told her to cut cedars from Minume-yama (Mikusa-yama in present Toyono District, Osaka) and make ships to ensure victory. On return, ships stopped offshore of this place, then a cape in antiquity; divination revealed it was the will of the Minume-yama deity, so Minume-no-Kami was enshrined here. This appears to preserve some historical truth. The ''{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}'' also records the female deities of Inagawa and {{ill|Muko River|Q6933569|qid=Q6933569}} competing for favor of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami|qid=Q1114013}}. Another ''Settsu no Kuni Fudoki'' excerpt says that before {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyouke Ōkami}} moved to {{ill|Tanba Province|Q954511|qid=Q954511}}, the deity resided at Inakura-yama in Settsu (location unknown), and one theory places this in the upper Inagawa area ({{ill|Toyono District, Osaka|Q1205516|qid=Q1205516}}?).

In the {{ill|Genba-ryō|Q11572314|qid=Q11572314}} section of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'', it is noted that when guests from {{ill|Silla|Q28456|qid=Q28456}} visited, sake brewed at {{ill|Ikuta Shrine|Q710086|qid=Q710086}} was served here. Since sake was also served at the {{ill|Kōrokan|Q11675677|qid=Q11675677}} in {{ill|Namba|Q1075406|qid=Q1075406}}, serving sake here was a kind of ritual. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', it is listed as “Minume Shrine, Yatabe District, Settsu Province,” ranked as a small shrine.

Because this was the first overnight harbor when traveling by ship westward from the capital through present {{ill|Ōsaka|Q11439906|qid=Q11439906}}, and also where {{ill|Mount Ikoma|Q996259|qid=Q996259}} and other views recalling {{ill|Yamato|Q13417196|qid=Q13417196}} emerged on return from the west, many poets - including {{ill|Kakinomoto no Hitomaro|Q380818|qid=Q380818}}, {{ill|Ōtomo no Tabito|Q386287|qid=Q386287}}, and {{ill|Tanabe no Sakimaro|Q11577372|qid=Q11577372}} - composed {{ill|Waka (poetry)|Q737148|qid=Q737148}} here. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, haikai poet {{ill|Yosa Buson|Q31523|qid=Q31523}} also visited repeatedly on his way to the Kitakaze house in Hyōgo.

Facing the {{ill|Seigoku kaidō|Q10518413|qid=Q10518413}} (Hama Kaidō), with various amusements, it was lively with worshippers from land and sea. In August Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) it was ranked village shrine; in September Shōwa 5 it was promoted to prefectural shrine. On June 5, Shōwa 20, shrine buildings were destroyed in war damage; rebuilt in Shōwa 27.

There used to be a spring beneath the hill of the main sanctuary, but it dried up in the {{ill|Damage by Great Hanshin earthquake|Q11392882|qid=Q11392882}}.

== God of severing ties ==
[[画像:Mirume-Jinja-mae-BusStop-20230504.jpg|thumb|200px|Nearest bus stop is read as “'''mirume''' jinja-mae”]]
Traditionally, bridal processions do not pass in front of this shrine for fear of divorce. It is said the goddess would be jealous, and the shrine is also known for rites of severing ties.

== Reading of “Minume” ==
As a shrine name, 敏馬 is read “mi'''nu'''me,” but the nearby Hanshin bus stops “Minume Jinja-mae” and “Minume” are read “mi'''ru'''me.” Meiji-Taishō documents show both readings<ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Latest Kinki Excursion Guide |date=1911-07|publisher=Naniwa Shobō |pages=Hanshin Electric Railway line 22 |author=Edited by Naniwa-kai}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Guide to Kobe Landmarks |date=1897-10|publisher=Kumagai Kueidō |page=7 |author=Kadokawa Monzō (Takagiyama-jin)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Centered on Kobe, Part 1 |year=1919|publisher=Akanishi Manyūdō |author=Edited by Harumichi Anji and Senjirō Fukuhara}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Man'yōshū Ryakukai 6 |year=1875|publisher=Katano Tōshirō |page=17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|和書 |title=Guide to Kobe Scenic Places: with nearby area |date=1897-04|publisher=Nittōkan |page=14 |author=Edited by Naoomi Nabeshima}}</ref>.
